provenance: Edition 1.2, reviewed 1 October 2026 at source revision ec07dd0. Working means accepted within the stated physical trial; Partial retains a material acceptance limit. Entries link the relevant dated evidence. Later live-session work is outside this pinned snapshot. Scores are editorial judgements, not measurements.

scale.functionality: How complete the behaviour is for someone using the device.
scale.implementation: How robust and general the underlying implementation is.

statuses.Working: Observed working on the physical device.

systems.reach: Boots to SpringBoard and an interactive home screen. Settings changes persist across a clean reboot.

The separate M68AP profile reaches its home screen with accepted touch, live Camera preview and saved VGA photos that reopen after a fresh boot. The PinePhone has an EG25-G modem; native telephony integration remains unaccepted.

features.note: N45 unlock and Settings interaction are accepted on the physical phone; the separate M68 home-screen result has its own record.
The M68AP build reaches its home screen on the device, from an isolated second system image.
Settings and two VGA JPEGs persist through checked clean reboots. Full data copies pass fsck; this does not establish sudden-power-loss durability.

features.environment: PinePhone QEMU controls; physical clean reboot
features.note: The watchdog passes deliberate panic and shutdown-stall controls in QEMU. Physical normal runs show petting and clean reboot; arbitrary hardware-hang recovery is unproven.
The original client's pixels reach the physical display.
A curved fade precedes blank; a Power tap restores the image.
The Settings slider drives the panel; its minimum stays visible above the backlight's duty-cycle floor.
Finger contacts from the panel's controller reach the UI through the original multitouch driver — tap, drag and slide-to-unlock.
Two simultaneous contacts reach the app; pinch-to-zoom works in Photos.
Power and Home reach the original HID path.
One M68 lock-screen TIFF saves and extracts to a pixel-identical PNG. A temporary pause was reported; capture latency and gallery visibility remain unmeasured.
Owner accepted upright, exposed preview. The reviewed baseline delivers 29.5 native frames/s and selects 7.9 distinct images/s; panel updates are a separate counter.
Two genuine 640 × 480 JPEGs and thumbnails save; preview resumes. Both JPEGs keep their hashes and reopen after a fresh boot.
Only genuine 640 × 480 sensor capture is accepted. Higher-resolution modes remain untested; VGA is not enlarged to claim a higher resolution.
Read-only physical AXP803 values publish through the original power-source service. Synthetic QEMU samples separately validate the original UI consumer.
At the recorded 500 mA input limit, bright-lockscreen median battery balance was −55 mA; blanked idle was +166 mA. Heavy-use endurance is unproven.
System suspend is not implemented.
The clock runs at its handoff frequency; a higher clock needs a regulator change that has not been made.
One paired physical replay reduces mean atomic traps by 98.50–99.91%. Mean frame gaps do not improve consistently; a UI speed multiplier is not established.
The audio codec path is not brought up.
No network interface is connected.
The board includes an EG25-G modem. Its native telephony service path is not integrated or accepted; No Service does not mean absent hardware.

roadmap.note: Boots natively to an interactive home screen on the PinePhone, with touch, camera, battery and screenshots.

roadmap.targets: App Store era, same silicon family
roadmap.note: Later userspaces on the same processor generation, once 1.x coverage is broad.
The destination: a different, newer ARMv7 core — closer to what the PinePhone's A53 runs natively.
